title: Trolley Exclusion Stake – Movable Obstruction
question: Your ball is lying beside a blue and white trolley exclusion stake. The stake does not interfere with your lie, stance or swing, but you believe your shot might strike it. The stake is easily removable. What is the correct ruling?

choices.text: You must leave the stake where it is because it doesn't interfere with your stance or swing.
You may remove the stake before playing because it is a movable obstruction.
You are entitled to free relief from the stake.
You may only remove the stake if your opponent agrees.

explanation: A blue and white trolley exclusion stake that can be moved is treated as a movable obstruction under Rule 15.2. Movable obstructions may be removed anywhere on the course. Free relief is not required unless the obstruction is immovable and interferes with your stroke, lie, stance or area of intended swing.
